mission_08: Implement rate-distortion theory, which characterizes the fundamental tradeoff between compression rate and allowable distortion in lossy compression. The rate-distortion function R(D) gives the minimum number of bits per source symbol needed to represent the source with average distortion at most D. For a Gaussian source with variance sigma^2 and squared-error distortion, R(D) = 0.5 * log2(sigma^2/D) for D <= sigma^2. The Blahut-Arimoto algorithm for rate-distortion computes R(D) for arbitrary sources and distortion measures through iterative optimization. Rate-distortion theory underpins JPEG, MP3, video codecs, and all modern lossy compression standards.
